evals.name: trigger-and-first-question
evals.prompt: I've got a DevOps interview coming up at a mid-size product company, senior level. Can you run me a quick mock interview - maybe 3 questions on Kubernetes and CI/CD? Ask them one at a time like a real interviewer would.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a mock-interview request and uses the skill. Resolves config (level=senior, tier=product, count~3, topic=core-devops) and confirms it back in one line. Tells the candidate the available commands (hint/pass/time check/stop). Asks exactly ONE scenario question, phrased in a realistic interviewer voice with a short setup. Does NOT reveal the answer, model points, or hints. Waits for the candidate to respond rather than continuing.
expectations: The response confirms the resolved interview configuration (senior level, product-company tier, ~3 questions, Kubernetes/CI-CD topic) back to the user in roughly one line before starting
The response tells the candidate the available in-interview commands (at least: hint, pass, stop)
The response poses exactly ONE interview question this turn, not a list of two or more questions
The single question is framed as a realistic scenario with 2-4 sentences of situational setup, not a bare 'Explain X' or 'What is Y' definitional prompt
The response does NOT include the model answer, a list of points a strong answer should cover, evaluation criteria, or an unsolicited hint
The response ends by handing over to the candidate and does not fabricate a candidate answer or continue to question 2
The question topic is within Kubernetes or CI/CD as requested
The opening sets expectations on session length or pacing (a rough minute estimate, or per-question time), not only the number of questions

evals.name: full-interview-mediocre-candidate
evals.prompt:
Let's do a mock interview. Senior SRE, product-company style, 2 questions on incident response and SLOs. You play the interviewer, I'll paste my answers. When I type 'END INTERVIEW' give me the full written debrief and save it.

Ready.

(For your first question, here is my answer:) "If latency spikes I'd open the dashboards, check whether there was a recent deploy, and roll it back if there was. Then I'd look at the database to see if it's slow."

(For any follow-ups on that, my answer is:) "I'm not totally sure - I guess I'd scale up the service and add more replicas."

(For your second question, here is my answer:) "For an SLO I'd probably target 99.9% uptime. I'd mostly alert on CPU and memory being high. I don't really know how to calculate an error budget."

END INTERVIEW
evals.expected_output: Runs the interview turn-based, then after END INTERVIEW produces a structured debrief with an honestly calibrated (not inflated) verdict, a 5-dimension score table, per-question breakdowns citing what the candidate said, a patterns section, and a prioritized study plan. Saves a session file and appends to mock-interview-log.md.
expectations: The interview is conducted turn-based: question 1 is asked and answered with at least one follow-up before question 2 is introduced (the transcript does not present both questions at once)

During the interview portion (before END INTERVIEW) the interviewer does not teach, correct, confirm, or praise the substance of the candidate's answers - only neutral acknowledgements and probing follow-ups
The debrief contains an explicit overall verdict that is one of: Strong Hire, Hire, Lean Hire, No Hire

The verdict is NOT 'Strong Hire' and NOT 'Hire' - the candidate's answers (vague incident triage, alerting on CPU/memory, not knowing error budgets) warrant 'Lean Hire' or 'No Hire' at a senior product bar

The debrief includes a table or clearly delineated list scoring all five rubric dimensions (technical depth & correctness, structured problem-solving, tradeoff & judgment, production & reliability mindset, communication) on a 1-5 scale
The per-question breakdown references specifics of what the candidate actually said (e.g. 'scale up / add replicas', 'alert on CPU and memory', 'target 99.9%', 'don't know error budget')

The per-question breakdown includes what a strong answer covers - e.g. for the SLO question: user-centric SLIs, error budget as (1 - target) of the window, burn-rate alerting; for the latency question: stabilize before diagnosing, saturation vs crash reasoning
The debrief includes a cross-question 'Patterns' (or equivalent) section identifying recurring themes
The debrief includes a prioritized study plan with between 3 and 6 ordered items, each naming a concrete gap
A file named mock-interview-log.md exists in the run's outputs directory and contains a table row for this session
A per-session detail file (under a mock-interview-sessions directory or similar) exists in the run's outputs directory
The interviewer stops probing a question once the candidate adds nothing new twice in a row - it does not fire a third or fourth follow-up at a stonewalling candidate

evals.name: company-name-mapping-and-save
evals.prompt:
quiz me for my amazon SRE interview, staff level, 2 scenario questions. i'll keep my answers short. after the 2nd one tell me how i did and save it so i can track my progress.

ready

answer 1: "I'd use a circuit breaker and retries with backoff. Add a queue between the services. Scale the downstream service."

answer 2: "Multi-region means deploy to two regions and use Route53 failover. Replicate the database. Test the failover sometimes."

that's all my answers, give me the feedback
evals.expected_output: Maps 'amazon' to the MANG tier, level=staff, count=2. MANG interview texture. Honest verdict calibrated to a MANG staff bar (short shallow answers -> No Hire or Lean Hire, ideally noting they'd fare better at a lower tier). Saves both a session detail file and a row in mock-interview-log.md and tells the user where.
expectations: The company 'amazon' is mapped to the MANG / FAANG-tier company tier (stated in the config confirmation, notes, or debrief)
The resolved config is staff level and 2 questions
The interviewer pushes past the candidate's initial 3-sentence answer at least once - asking for quantification, a failure mode, or 'what breaks at scale' - rather than accepting it and moving on
The debrief contains an explicit overall verdict that is one of: Strong Hire, Hire, Lean Hire, No Hire
The verdict is 'No Hire' or 'Lean Hire' for the MANG staff bar (the answers lack quantification, depth, and rigor expected at that bar)
The debrief includes scores for all five rubric dimensions on a 1-5 scale

The per-question breakdown names what a strong answer covers - e.g. retry budgets / jitter / load shedding / circuit breaker half-open for Q1; DR-vs-active-active, RTO/RPO, the database as the hard part, split-brain, failover testing for Q2
The debrief includes a prioritized study plan with 3 to 6 items
A file named mock-interview-log.md exists in the run's outputs directory with a row for this session
A per-session detail file exists in the run's outputs directory
The response tells the user where the session was saved (a file path or directory is mentioned)
The interviewer stops probing a question once the candidate adds nothing new twice in a row - it does not fire a third or fourth follow-up at a stonewalling candidate
